objective.statement: Write rests for part of a beat so that no rest runs across a beat line.
successCriteria: I know a rest stops at the end of its beat.
I know to start a new rest for the next beat.
I can fix a rest that crosses a beat line.

explanation.text: Sometimes only part of a beat is silent. A quaver in 2/4 is half a crotchet beat, so a quaver rest fills the other half.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 2/4: a quaver, a quaver rest, then a crotchet.

explanation.caption: A quaver and a quaver rest together fill the first beat.

explanation.text: If the silence runs from part of one beat into the next, it needs a rest for each beat. A single rest must not stretch across the beat line.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 2/4: a quaver, then two quaver rests, then a quaver.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: quaver, quaver rest, quaver rest, quaver.

explanation.caption: Right: the silence between the two quavers is two quaver rests, one before and one after the beat line.

explanation.text: A crotchet rest in that gap would start in the middle of beat 1 and finish in the middle of beat 2: it hides where beat 2 begins.
Finish the rest for this beat, then start a new rest for the next beat.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 2/4: a quaver, two quaver rests, a quaver.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: quaver, quaver rest, quaver rest, quaver.

steps: The first beat is a quaver and a quaver rest.
The second beat starts with another quaver rest, then a quaver.
No rest crosses the beat line, so each beat is clear.

mistakes.compound-beat-hidden: In compound time each beat is a dotted note split into three. Group in threes so each beat shows.
